findings.reason: the section must instruct the node to broaden `declared_section_identities` (the owner) and point the four ref sites and `declared_for` at it, not author a parallel helper; authoring a second helper is the fork the item exists to prevent.
findings.text: §15 proposes "one helper beside plan_section_anchors that returns a plan's full section identity set" (plan.html s15), whose set is exactly "the gate and comment anchors, the section_declarations keys and the typed section record ids" — that helper already exists as `declared_section_identities` (reckon/_schema.py:678), which unions `plan_section_anchors(plan)`, the `section_declarations` mapping and the typed records from `plan["sections"]`, and is already consumed by `reckon/_store.py:2770` (feeding `decision_section_refusals`) and `reckon/roadmap.py:2601`

findings.reason: the plan must name one owner to keep (relocating `_declared_stages` beside `plan_section_anchors` in `_schema.py`, or deleting it in favour of `declared_section_identities`) so `declared_for` and the ref sites cannot drift into counting different populations of the same set.
findings.text: census of the same defect type: the identity-union already has two implementations, `reckon/_schema.py:678 declared_section_identities` and `reckon/roadmap.py:181 _declared_stages` (which §15 shows it saw, spelling it `_declared_stages` in the `declared_for` sentence), and §15 adds a third; the plan's own text says `_declared_stages` "unions ... with the declaration keys" and does not say which of the three survives

findings.reason: misclassifying the one site that already does the right thing means the node would "audit" the correct owner into staying wrong, and the fix as written would leave a duplicate owner behind.
findings.text: §15's audit clause lists `_schema.py:692` among the sites to "leave on anchors unless it validates existence" (plan.html s15), but line 692 is the body of `declared_section_identities`, whose stated purpose is to validate section existence for the decision-scope path (`decision_section_refusals` via `reckon/_store.py:2770`); leaving it on `plan_section_anchors` reproduces for decision scopes for decision scopes exactly the defect §15 reports for dependency refs

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend `declared_section_identities` and route the four ref sites plus `declared_for` through it; the wrapper exists only because the owner was not found.
findings.text: the proposed helper adds no behaviour `plan_section_anchors`, `declared_section_identities` or `_declared_stages` lacks; §15 gives no justification that the existing machinery cannot be extended

findings.reason: resolving the duplicate_owner finding (broaden `declared_section_identities`, do not add a helper) removes the added definition entirely, so the interface-budget remedy is the same edit as the owner-extension fix and does not change the plan a second time.
findings.text: public_definitions 1506, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §15's "one helper beside plan_section_anchors" is a new public module-level definition and the section names nothing it retires or merges and states no reason nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §15 is sound as a shape (one set answers "does this section exist"), but it introduces a new module-level helper whose whole body is a union already performed by two existing functions, so it is surface without depth rather than a deep module hiding the set-membership rule.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements the declared-section helper rather than extending its owner (`reckon/_schema.py:678`), and a second copy (`reckon/roadmap.py:181 _declared_stages`) already exists, so the change would leave three owners of one set.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1506, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §15 adds a public module-level definition (`one helper`) and names nothing it retires or merges, and nothing in the plan's own text explains why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §15 cites `plan_section_anchors`, `declared_for`, `_declared_stages` and every `plan_section_anchors` call site, but misses `declared_section_identities` (`reckon/_schema.py:678`), the existing owner that already returns the full authored section-identity set, so the search that concludes "author one helper" was run without finding the machinery that already is that helper.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the proposed "one helper beside plan_section_anchors" forwards to `plan_section_anchors` plus the declaration keys plus the typed-record ids, and §15 states no reason the existing owner (`reckon/_schema.py:678`) cannot be extended instead.
